newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian Dec palm oil output seen down by 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian Dec palm oil output seen down by 15 pct.

text.p: Malaysian December palm oil production is estimated to have fallen by up to 15 percent compared with November, plantation houses said on Monday.
Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA), which is scheduled to release December crop data on January 16, said November's palm oil output was 762,540 tonnes.
"The further drop in output for December is expected as it was mainly because of a seasonal downtrend and unfavourable weather conditions," an official at one plantation house said.
The largest drop came mainly from the East Malaysian state of Sabah, traders said.

Ivan Wong, a crop forecaster, said in his last report that tighter supplies were caused by poorer-than-expected output in Sabah because of monsoon rains and floods which struck the state on the island of Borneo in the last week of December.
Tropical storm Greg killed 209 people and caused damages to property in Sabah.

However, Wong said there was a marked improvement in the weather so far this month in Penisular Malaysia and the east Malaysian states, indicating that the monsoon was over and the seasonal downtrend in production this month should moderate.
Wong will release his latest December crop data on January 14. Traders had earlier projected end-December stocks at 805,000 tonnes against end-November's 955,965 tonnes.
Exports in December were estimated at between 660,000 and 680,000 tonnes, against PORLA's 632,441 tonnes in November.
-- Tan Lee Lee, Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230-7510)
